script: "They booked a day early, then betrayed us—my staff was STUNNED by the fallout!". My submissions have been aplenty lately as the people continue to surprise me. Today, I walked into quite the kerfuffle, where a couple who accidentally showed up a day late wanted us to take responsibility for that happening. Right after the bell rang, the place was already buzzing. The Cakes, a couple who'd booked a day early by mistake, stormed in. They were basically saying, "We're here for tomorrow, but you cancelled us because you're sold out." Mr. Cake, the big guy, was already pulling out a phone, like, "I get the policy, but how the hell did you not call me?" I am talking about a hotel with a few hundred rooms, not some boutique with 10. If this was a tiny place, maybe we'd ping everyone. But here, people are just… well, we're not that tiny. Still, they were all "pleasant" but still venting about our "apparent lack of care." The conversation spilled into the lobby, and they didn't even leave. The group was a full crew. Some members were in the lobby, chatting, while Mr. Cake was ranting about how they "gave away" our room and didn't even bother to call. He compared us to a high-tier loyalty brand with a dedicated hotline. Classic. After a few minutes, the group leader came up, eyes bright, and declared, "I worked my magic! You've got your room!" She'd gone to the sales agent, grabbed a cancellation slot, and re‑instated their reservation. They had been hanging around for about 40 minutes. Even after the fix, Mr. Cake kept bringing up the whole ordeal. He laughed at the explanation that a cancellation saved the day. He didn't even check his confirmation email until we asked. Accountability? Yeah, that's a trend now. That's the whole tea, bestie.
